provenance.what: Eighth live run: both golden sets under prompt v4, whose rule 10 is an identity guard. Motivated by a real-corpus field transcript: asked 'whaat can you do for me?', the assistant escalated to a frontier rung and answered AS the company in the documents - grounded, cited, and spoken by the wrong voice, presenting the corpus's products as its own abilities; a follow-up 'do you summarize documents?' paid for a second call and then refused. The fix is three-layered: the corpus tier's you-frame now answers capability and identity questions free of any model call (pinned by unit tests on the verbatim field questions), rule 10 guards the answers that do reach a model, and this run proves the new rule costs nothing on both golden sets - accuracy, determinism and paraphrase consistency all hold at 1.0 with zero false answers.
provenance.models: Chat: Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 Q4_K_M via llama-cpp-python. Embeddings: nomic-embed-text v1.5 Q4_K_M, task prefixes applied.
provenance.corpus: evals/corpus/aveline in full (11 documents); companion run on the repository documents/
provenance.hardware: 4-core CPU container, no GPU; both model servers local
provenance.caveat: These sets ask about the documents, not about the assistant, so this run proves rule 10 does no harm - the do-no-harm bar every prompt change must clear. The behaviour it fixes was measured in the field on a frontier rung and is pinned by the corpus-tier unit tests; the you-frame answers those questions before any model sees them.
